title: Credential-access tooling staged and executed from C:\Windows\Temp on nashua
rationale: F66 describes attacker tooling (python.exe, Rar.exe, sdelete64.exe) dropped into and executed from C:\Windows\Temp on nashua.dmevals.local by user pbeesly, driven by PsExec and PowerShell, performing credential-file discovery and wiping the collected credential archive. This is a distinct action (tool staging and execution on nashua). The best-fitting in-scope technique is T1003 (OS Credential Dumping), as labeled.

title: LSASS memory access with full-access masks by PowerShell and wsmprovhost (scranton and nashua)
rationale: All these findings describe the same attacker action: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, user pbeesly) on scranton.dmevals.local opening lsass.exe (PID 736) with GrantedAccess 0x1F3FFF and 0x1FFFFF at 2020-05-02T03:05:16, and the related wsmprovhost.exe opening lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF on nashua.dmevals.local at 03:09:29. The shared events (AaFHM31uOFchItTka0Gm, AaFHM31uOFchItTka0Gj, AaFHNH1uOFchItUHCTY0) and the identical action on the same hosts confirm one incident. The best-fitting in-scope technique is T1003.001 (LSASS Memory), since the observed action is reading LSASS process memory with full-access masks. Findings F13, F19, F24, F26, F51 were reported under other technique labels (T1056.004, T1110.002, T1111, T1212, T1558) but their own summaries state the action is credential dumping from LSASS memory, not the labeled technique.

title: Malicious screensaver cod.3aka3.scr drives PowerShell credential-access chain on scranton
rationale: F12 describes the execution of C:\ProgramData\victim\cod.3aka3.scr via explorer.exe on scranton.dmevals.local, spawning cmd.exe and powershell.exe, and accessing the LSA registry key. This is a distinct action (initial execution of the malicious screensaver) from the LSASS access incident. The best-fitting in-scope technique is T1056 (Input Capture), as the finding is labeled and the screensaver drives the credential-access chain.

title: PowerShell steganographic loader and shellcode injector on scranton
rationale: F14 describes the PowerShell steganographic loader reading monkey.png and IEX'ing decoded payload plus shellcode injection on scranton.dmevals.local. F65 describes the PyInstaller python.exe on nashua.dmevals.local performing credential discovery and anti-forensic wiping, which is part of the same tooling chain (both labeled T1056.001). These share the credential-access tooling action. The best-fitting in-scope technique is T1056.001 (Keylogging), as labeled, though the observed action is payload delivery and discovery.

title: PowerShell Invoke-Exfil credential-handling exfiltration script on scranton
rationale: F23 describes the Invoke-Exfil PowerShell script on scranton.dmevals.local that compresses the Downloads folder, builds a PSCredential from hardcoded credentials, and copies the archive to a WebDAV share. This is a distinct action (exfiltration with credential use). The finding is labeled T1111 (Multi-Factor Authentication Interception), which is the best-fitting in-scope technique per the finding's own label, though the summary notes it does not demonstrate MFA interception.

title: Sysinternals accesschk.exe run and passwordsDB file on scranton
rationale: F31 describes accesschk.exe run and the passwordsDB file on scranton.dmevals.local, and F64 describes credential-file harvesting and password-protected exfil archive on nashua.dmevals.local. Both are labeled T1552.001 (Credentials In Files) and describe credential/secret harvesting from files on disk. The best-fitting in-scope technique is T1552.001.

title: PowerShell Get-PrivateKeys exports all LocalMachine private keys to .pfx files on scranton
rationale: F30 and F61 both describe the same action: user pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local executing the Get-PrivateKeys PowerShell script that enumerates cert:\LocalMachine and exports every certificate with a private key to randomly-named .pfx files protected with the hardcoded password 'saribas'. They share the same script block event (AaFHNX1uOFchItZSl2ML) and the resulting .pfx file (AaFHM31uOFchItTkbEF9). The best-fitting in-scope technique is T1552.004 (Private Keys).

title: Malicious intrusion chain on scranton with credential use and exfiltration
rationale: F39 describes the full intrusion chain on scranton.dmevals.local: cod.3aka3.scr execution, PowerShell steganographic payload, sdclt.exe UAC-bypass, and Invoke-Exfil compressing Downloads into OfficeSupplies.7z. This is a distinct summary finding of the overall chain. The best-fitting in-scope technique is T1555 (Credentials from Password Stores), as labeled, though the summary notes no password-store theft was observed.

title: PsExec lateral movement with cleartext credentials (scranton to nashua)
rationale: F11, F20, and F60 all describe the same action: user pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local running PsExec64.exe against \\NASHUA with cleartext credentials (-u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by), launching C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on nashua.dmevals.local, with PSEXESVC service installs and 4648 explicit-credential logons. This is lateral movement (T1021 Remote Services), not credential access, so the technique is out-of-scope:T1021.
